This is getting into “what is art” category, but for the most part when it comes to nudity it is acceptable when it’s got a purpose and it’s tasteful. A caricature of a penis is not tasteful. Not that it’s not art, or not funny or whatever, it’s just juvenile. And it’s also worth mentioning that pretty much any art hosting website that isn’t trying to be a porn site has rules for what is and isn’t tasteful nude and I’m pretty sure most of not all of them would not put yours into “tasteful”. 

I think it’s kind of ridiculous that female nudity is so often used as lighting study or artistic expression but rarely this is true for male nudity. Meaning you often see these paintings of butt naked women strewn out of a bed of satin with dynamic lighting but you almost never see similar drawings or paintings of nude men. I’ve of course seen some (and I LOVE them) but it’s rare and it’s obviously bullshit that the subjects are so often naked women. Yes, they’re beautiful, but come on if we’re using a nude figure as the subject it’s stupid that it’s almost always a woman. 

The better thing to have done would have been to draw basically the exact same thing as the other person, but a man. 

Instead, you drew a caricature of a penis and sure it’s entertaining to look at, but it doesn’t sound like you’re stretching yourself artistically or playing with certain skills. Drawing human anatomy is a complicated skill in and of itself and so there is merit to drawing a nude figure- not so much a penis- not that it doesn’t take skill. The other issue is that it’s supposed to be funny as a baseline. Most people will look at a tasteful nude piece and mostly be drawn in my the smoothness or texture of the skin or the anatomy or whatever. Your penis was a joke. Literally. That was the point. 

And I don’t like art classes, particularly the high school variety so I’m not 100% what the point of “free draw” is but I’m pretty sure the teacher is trying to get you to use skills he’s been trying to teach you to create a piece. To play with the things you’ve been taught. You instead drew a joke and on top of it not being appropriate for a high school class, probably seems like you’re not taking the teacher or his class seriously.

You’ve been re-reading your older writing? I was stuck in a not improving rut and decided to dig up some of my older stuff and oh buddy I am improving it’s just hard to see it as you’re doing it. You have to compare and contrast.

Also, if this is first draft stuff it’s okay for it to sound clunky. Being able to identify clunkiness or other flaws in our writing leads to improvement. The more you write the better you get at identifying where your writing is shitty. It’s a natural point where you go “damn I’m *bad* at this”. It happens and this is absolutely a good thing it just feels awful. Next you’ll get to a point where you not only can identify bad writing but *why* it’s bad, and how to fix it. This same thing happens with painters and artists and lots of other creative mediums. This is the hard part. Stop, do some reading, think about how other writers avoid things you feel like you’re doing wrong. Don’t let yourself fall into “I’ll never be as good as that”, just dissect it and try to apply it to your own work. If you really get into a scene, ask yourself why and what accomplished that, then look at you’re own writing to see if that is missing.

I went to summer school a lot because I was garbage at school. I went to a ton of different schools, so I experienced a bunch of different school’s summer school. 

All of mine were a month long, Monday to Friday and only a couple of hours. Typically 8am to noon. There is an entirely different atmosphere in summer school, *no one* wants to be there and everyone is tired so it’s very muted. The teacher tries to quickly assess what the class missed so they can condense the information you need to obtain. They cover entire sections of the class very quickly and work one on one with the students. They make sure everyone fully understands the material and often times the class will come to a halt so the teacher can spend 15+ minutes explaining something to one student so you spend plenty of time zoning out if you’ve got the material down. There are a lot of tests but they’re low stakes, the teacher comes around to help you if they notice you don’t get it. They’ll even give you hints on what you’ve messed up but won’t answer the questions for you. It’s way more hands on than typical class and you get plenty of time with the teacher.

If you have any other specific questions about summer school or anything else, feel free to ask.

I took mostly Math summer courses because I struggled with it most, but I did take one English summer school. They cut out all the big things and just tried to prove we had an understanding of the things we’d be tested on. They’d take the curriculum and condense it down to what each things was teaching and making sure you understood it. There was no homework so everything happened in class. We used articles, poems and essays for reading material and all of it would be relatively short, less than 5 pages. We were tested on essays so we had to write a few, vocabulary, grammar, etc and the majority of the work in summer school classes are work pages and tests. We had to write an essay along with our final test at the end of summer school. 

Typically you’d know nearing the end of the school year that you’d be ending up in summer school. If you were sent to summer school because you had too many missed days for that course then you’d know as soon as you hit the threshold of too many missed days. For failing the class, the teacher would let you know as soon as they noticed you were on the trajectory for summer school. Sometimes you skirt by for the majority of the year and in the last two months your teacher would offer you opportunities to get your grade up. 

It’s worth mentioning that sometimes you can find out a little last minute if something happens with missing classes or if you transferred enough times, they might notice a credit you earned from another school doesn’t qualify as a credit for your school and you’ll be told you needed to take summer school pretty late. You could be on track to barely pass the class but something goes wrong and you miss your test and can’t make it up. Some teachers are complete jerks and won’t afford you any opportunities to make things up or even keep you in the loop. A few times I found out I was going to summer school right around the last week of school. Summer school begins the immediate Monday after the last day of the school year. 

Report cards are given after each semester normally. So you’d get one sometime in early-mid January and another at the end of the school year. I remember being sent home with my end of the year report card and it being mailed to my parents. It was always fun to end the school year off and then a day later get grounded. 

And no, summer school for public school is free. It is paid for by the school’s budget. For private schools you might have to pay but as far as I know private schools have summer courses as an opt in.

I write and draw so I can actually draw up my characters but I don’t think being “good” at drawing is really a factor. 

I sit down and do a very basic sketch of a character, almost a T-Pose drawing where I just slap on some clothes, pick kind of what their hair looks like and determine if their hair and eyes are dark or light. The clothes are the big one because clothes kind of say something about an individual. I can easily describe this stuff instead of draw it, of course. Then I pick a generic ass name even if the character is going to a high fantasy story, the name is just a working name so I know what to call them. If a character is already fitting a role within the story, I have a ballpark of what they would probably look like/dress like. An army general is not going to be anything like a 16 year old kid. 

If I don’t already have a story for them, I start building the story alongside them, or at least a story for them to dick around in until they have an actual place to go. I have a basic feel for their personality, because of the way they dress and do their hair, so I have something to go on. As I do the same to the other characters the questions of how these characters interact and feel about each other answers itself. If one character hates another, that says something about them. The character should influence the story and the story should influence the character. Now I’ve got a basic idea of who, I ask why. What is the character’s backstory and how did that backstory produce this character. By doing this I end up with a character that doesn’t truly reflect the product of what made them, so they get redesigned. Now is when I start adding in bigger things, what race are they? Where are they from? Does their backstory and race combination lead to unfortunate negative stereotypes? A character without a father figure is one thing, a black boy without a father is a particular stereotype. Will I remove that or are there other characters in my story that are black and have good father figures, showing that this world isn’t one where all black kids don’t have dads? 

By this point their appearance and who they are, are connected. Even if the character doesn’t look like what you’d think they should look like, that says something about them. I feel as if our appearances are deeply connected to our sense of self and how we view ourselves. Even if I never talk about a character’s nose and how they’re insecure about it in the story, I know they are, I know why they’re insecure and I know what that says about the character. And as I go back and forth, tweaking the backstory against how they look I end up really knowing this character and why they act the way they do. 

Another thing I stop and decide, because I feel like it’s particularly insightful is decide what a character’s sense of humor is. Do they like slapstick? Do they like dark humor? Are they into play on words? Another random one is flavor, do they prefer bitter? Are they stuck up about liking bitter things or do they really just enjoy the flavor? Maybe they like sour things because sour is fun, or spicy because spicy is adventurous. Or they’re a comfort food person. There are so many little weird things you can focus on that says something about a character and helps you identify who they are and why they are. 

Hopefully that helps?
